name: Ottoman Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "Ottoman Empire" = 2.26M km2 on the sphere; it includes the Danubian principalities and lacks parts of Arabia and Libya. Directly ruled lands in 1877 (Rumelia, Bosnia, Anatolia, Syria, Iraq, Hejaz, Yemen, Tripolitania) ~2.6-3.2M km2.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1877 = 34,323k, which appears to include autonomous Egypt (~6-7M). Without Egypt, Romania and Serbia: Anatolia ~11-12M (OWID Turkey 1877 = 12.2M), Rumelia and Bosnia ~6M, Arab provinces and Libya ~7-8M = ~25-26M.

activePersonnel.note: Russo-Turkish War page: Allen and Muratoff total 378,000 (168,000 under Abdulkerim at Shumla, 140,000 in Europe, 45,000 garrisons, 70,000 Caucasus); Olender: regular army 400,000 plus 90,000 irregular and Egyptian troops. COW milper 1877 = 461,000.

trainedReserves.note: Redif and mustahfiz still mobilising in spring 1877 (page: on paper 571 battalions, 441,954 infantry).

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery ~20,000 (143 batteries, page), engineers and train, navy ~15,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: Muslim men only were conscripted; ~700,000 served in 1877-78; the 1914-18 effort later reached ~2.8M of ~21M.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Page (Olender): 571 infantry battalions (181 nizam), 441,954 on paper incl. 140,094 nizam; regular field infantry ~300,000 after garrisons and mobilisation gaps.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: 75% armed with Peabody-Martini (accurate to 1,800 yards), 300,000 bought before the war; Winchester repeaters for some (page)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: nizam solid, redif poorly trained; excellent entrenching

count.note: Irregulars (bashi-bazouks, Circassians) and Egyptian contingents; page: 90,000 irregular and Egyptian troops.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mixed old rifles

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: undisciplined irregulars

count.note: Page (Olender): 147 squadrons = 21,021 regular cavalry on paper; Circassian irregular horse in addition.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Winchester carbines

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: squadrons ~100 men in practice (page)

count.note: Page (Olender): 143 batteries = 858 guns on paper, excluding fortress companies.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Krupp 8 cm and 9 cm C/73 field guns (page)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: outnumbered and poorly concentrated

count.note: Ottoman Navy page: in 1875 the navy had 21 battleships (ironclads) and 173 other warships, the third largest navy in the world. Turret ship Luetf-ue Celil lost on the Danube in May 1877 (Russo-Turkish War page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: British- and French-built ironclads of the 1860s-70s

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: laid-up fleet after the 1875 bankruptcy, passive in 1877

count.note: Corvettes, gunboats and the Danube flotilla; many of the 173 other vessels of 1875 were transports or obsolete.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: river monitors and gunboats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: sunk by Russian and Romanian torpedo boats and batteries on the Danube

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Osman Pasha at Plevna and Muhtar Pasha in the Caucasus able; Abdulkerim passive, Istanbul interference

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: tenacious Anatolian conscripts in defence, irregulars unreliable

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: defensive war, victories over Serbia in 1876, Plevna

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: Peabody-Martini and Krupp breech-loaders outranged the Russian Krnka (page)

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: none on land

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: large ironclad fleet

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Plevna earthworks, Danube quadrilateral fortresses, Kars

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: little railway, pack animals

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: telegraph to the fortresses

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID): Turkey (modern borders) 1870 = 1,165; analogues Bulgaria 1870 = 1,339, Egypt 1870 = 1,195.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: COW milex 1876 = 19,710 (thousands of pounds) for a bankrupt state (1875 default); war spending financed by paper money (kaime).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: crafts and a few state factories.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: grain from Rumelia and Anatolia.

annualCohort.note: Analogue ratio of the France 1805 snapshot (~1.05% of population a year) applied to the ~60-65% Muslim share eligible for conscription; high = whole population.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Tophane arsenal output per year; most guns imported from Krupp.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: engineered roads in Rumelia and western Anatolia.

railKm.note: Educated guess: reconstruction: Oriental Railways in Rumelia ~1,180 km by 1874, Varna-Rustchuk 224 km, Banja Luka line ~100 km, Izmir lines ~400 km, Haydarpasa-Izmit 91 km.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Constantinople, Smyrna, Salonica, Varna, Batumi, Trebizond, Beirut, Basra.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: mostly sailing craft owned by Greek and Muslim merchants.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: pack trains and few roads.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses, mules, oxen and camels.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: fortress system and Muslim population support; Balkan Christians hostile.

notes: Snapshot = Ottoman Empire in April 1877 (Russian declaration of war). Territory and population = directly ruled provinces (Rumelia, Bosnia, Anatolia, Arab provinces, Tripolitania); Egypt, Romania, Serbia and Montenegro excluded; includes is empty. Border uses world_1815 (nearest file at or before 1877), which includes the Danubian principalities. Personnel: nizam and mobilised redif = active; remaining redif and mustahfiz = trainedReserves; irregulars as infantry_light. Strengths from the Russo-Turkish War page (Allen and Muratoff; Olender) and the Ottoman Navy page; rail, merchant fleet and population split are reconstructions (grade C/D).
